correctness.rationale: With Fourier normalization F_alpha(t)=2∫_0^1(1−x)^alpha cos(tx)dx, direct integration gives F_1(t)=2(1−cos t)/t² and positive double roots T_n=2πn. Differentiating in alpha at 1 gives 2[γ+log T_n−Ci(T_n)]/T_n² with positive C_n=∫_0^{T_n}(1−cos u)/u du, hence local Taylor F_{1−ε}(T_n+s)=(s²−2C_n ε)/T_n²+O_n(|s|³+ε|s|+ε²). Fixed-index implicit-function roots are ±sqrt(2C_n ε)+O_n(ε), exactly two per cell by positivity away from T_n. The exact lower-incomplete-gamma formula and standard DLMF 8.11 upper incomplete-gamma asymptotics give uniformly for alpha near1 F_alpha(t)/2=alpha t^(−2)+Γ(alpha+1)t^(−alpha−1)cos(t−π(alpha+1)/2)+O(t^(−4)), uniformly with s derivative. For n→∞ and ε log(2πn)→λ∈(0,∞), this scales to 1−e^λ cos s on the entire bounded cell [-π,π], with exactly two simple zeros at ±arccos(e^(−λ)); uniform C^1 convergence yields exact two-zero assertion. Independently evaluated exact mpmath incomplete-gamma integral at 50-digit precision for n=1,3,10 with ε=1e−5, confirming local square-root coefficients and for n=10^5,10^7 at λ=.5 confirming convergence toward ±0.919106657294. The finite numerics are corroboration; analytic uniform estimate and compactness establish all sequences. Actual source RESULT.md, check.py and checker output listing were compared.

evidence: Tuck applies when alpha>1 through convexity; Sedletskii treats fixed increasing weight alpha<1; neither controls n exponential in 1/ε. DLMF provides gamma kernel expansion but no root-tracking theorem by itself.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new conclusion requires combining singular perturbation at T_n with uniform endpoint asymptotics and C^1 convergence in logarithmically scaled cells, not mere substitution of an existing fixed-alpha zero location result.

evidence: The power-tent cosine transform reduces via integration by parts to a sine transform of an increasing weight when alpha<1; Pólya/Sedletskii qualitative zero theorems apply.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Those qualitative real/simple zero placements are not equivalent to a derivative-in-alpha double-zero unfolding or the ε log n arccos limit for every admissible sequence.

originality.rationale: Tuck 2006 is the qualitative convex Fourier-transform positivity theorem; his actual six-page primary paper was read in full, and contains no alpha→1 fractional-tent paired-root crossover. Sedletskii 2009 treats qualitative location/realness of sine/cosine zeros for positive increasing weights, without the two-parameter logarithmic limit in accessible abstract. DLMF §8.11 provides the classical incomplete gamma expansion used in proof; that is a shared lemma, not the claimed application. Bounded searches did not identify an exact fixed-index square-root plus all-sequences logarithmic arccos transition; general finite Fourier transform zero literature could contain equivalent formulas.
residual_risks: Potential earlier equivalent double-scaling analysis in classical non-English Fourier-transform zero literature was not comprehensively ruled out.
Uniformity excludes crossover endpoints λ=0 and λ=∞ and any claims about complex zeros; numerical checks alone cannot certify the uniform theorem.

value.rationale: The exponent alpha=1 is an authentic double-zero coalescence separating Fourier positivity and oscillation, and the natural nonuniform parameter ε log T controls when infinitesimal exponent changes persist at exponentially high frequencies. Explicit fixed-n square-root unfolding and arccos crossover classify a sharp transition that qualitative positivity or pointwise-in-alpha asymptotics do not quantify. This is a motivated precise Fourier zero invariant rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.

limitations: α approaches 1 strictly from below; fixed positive n or sequences with ε log(2πn)→λ in (0,∞).
Fourier transform uses the stated even compact-support convention; exactly two real zeros in each stipulated open cell, no full complex-zero classification.
